decision.trend: The trend in the research is to explore the effects of processing routes and alloy composition on the microstructure and mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs). Earlier studies have focused on the development of HEAs with promising mechanical properties, but the individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. Recent studies have investigated the use of various processing routes, such as selective laser melting (SLM), spark plasma sintering (SPS), and hot isostatic pressing (HIP), to improve the microstructure and mechanical properties of HEAs.
decision.unsolved: The unsolved problem is to understand the effects of changing the percentage of elements on the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA. The individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored, and the optimal composition and processing route to achieve the desired mechanical properties are still unknown.
decision.why: A controlled variable experiment is the most plausible next step to investigate the effects of changing the percentage of elements on the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA. By systematically varying the composition of the alloy, researchers can identify the individual constituents' effects and optimize the composition to achieve the desired mechanical properties. This approach is supported by earlier studies, such as PMC5578249 and PMC6926650, which have demonstrated the importance of composition and processing route on the microstructure and mechanical properties of HEAs.
